- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) and price is falling, model frequently undercorrects; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias to avoid mean reversion lag.
- In low-sentiment periods (sentiment <0.3 for 3+ days), model tends to overestimate mean reversion; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid premature bottoming.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.6) and price is volatile, model often fails to capture short-term reversals; apply 0.5–1.0% smoothing filter to avoid overfitting to recent noise.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price by 1–3% in low-sentiment environments; add 1–2% upward bias if sentiment <0.4.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model often fails to capture momentum; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% above trendline.
